text.tspan: Spot requests and Spot Fleets
Spot request
you set: max price, number of instances,
launch spec, type: one-time or persistent,
valid from / until
if spot price > your max price: you get a
2-minute notice, then stop or terminate
One-time request
fulfilled once, then the request closes
Persistent request
relaunches instances when they are stopped
Trap: to stop spot instances for good
1. CANCEL the spot request first
(only open, active or disabled
requests can be cancelled)
2. then TERMINATE the instances
If you terminate first, a persistent
request just launches new ones.
Spot Fleet = a set of Spot Instances + (optional) On-Demand Instances, from several launch pools
(pools = instance type + OS + AZ). It tries to meet the target capacity within your price limit.
Allocation strategies:
• lowestPrice: cheapest pool (cost optimisation, short workloads)
• diversified: spread across all pools (great for availability and long workloads)
• capacityOptimized: pools with the most spare capacity (fewer interruptions)
• priceCapacityOptimized (recommended): most capacity first, then the lowest price among those
